app.name: FleetWise
app.tagline: Every machine on your farm — costs, services, faults, in one place.

auth.checkEmail: Check your email for the sign-in link.
auth.welcomeSub: Sign in to manage your farm's machines.
auth.noEmailBody: You don't need one. Scan the QR sticker on any machine to report a problem or write down the hours — no login at all.
auth.errInvalid: That email or password isn't right. Check them and try again.
auth.errNotConfirmed: This account hasn't been opened yet. Use the link in your invite email.
auth.errRate: Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again.
auth.errGeneric: That didn't work. Try again, or ask the farm office to re-send your invite.

onboarding.title: Get your farm set up
onboarding.subtitle: A few quick steps to get the most out of FleetWise.
onboarding.allDone: You're all set up — nice work!
onboarding.step1Desc: Add each tractor, bakkie, harvester and implement — or import them all from a spreadsheet.
onboarding.step2Desc: Apply a service template to each machine so FleetWise knows when a service is due.
onboarding.step3Desc: Print a QR sticker for each machine and stick it on. This is the bit that makes the whole thing work — anyone who can hold a phone can then report a problem or write down the hours, with no login.
onboarding.step4Desc: Add your manager and mechanic so job cards and faults are captured as work happens.
onboarding.step3Hint: Print them on plain paper and tape them somewhere dry — inside the cab door works well.

machines.name: Name / nickname
machines.emptyHint: Adjust the filters, or add your first machine.

privacy.title: Data & privacy (POPIA)
privacy.intro: Export or erase a person's personal data on request. An export returns everything we hold on them; erasure anonymises their identity while keeping legally-required history.
privacy.eraseConfirm: Erase this person's personal data? Their name, email and phone are cleared and the account is deactivated. Maintenance, cost and AARTO driver-usage history is kept but de-identified. This cannot be undone.
privacy.erased: Personal data erased and the account deactivated.
privacy.retentionNote: Driver-usage (AARTO) records are retained under a legal obligation even after erasure — see docs/POPIA.md.
privacy.eraseIntro: This is the one thing on the farm you cannot undo. Only do it if {name} has asked you to, in writing.
privacy.eraseWhatHappens: What happens the moment you press it
privacy.eraseEffect1: Their name, email and phone number are wiped from every job card, reading and fault
privacy.eraseEffect2: They can never sign in again
privacy.eraseEffect3: The work itself stays — it just has no name on it
privacy.eraseReversibleHint: Just want them out of the system? Turn their login off instead — that one you can undo.

confirm.whatHappens: What happens when you press it
confirm.softDeleteNote: Nothing is really erased — it stops showing on this machine and stays in the farm's history.
confirm.deleteServiceLineIntro: This is one of the service jobs FleetWise watches for on {machine}.
confirm.deleteServiceLineEffect1: FleetWise stops working out when this job is next due
confirm.deleteServiceLineEffect2: Nobody gets reminded about it again — not by alert, not on the board
confirm.deleteKitIntro: This is the parts list you apply to a job card on {machine}.
confirm.deleteKitEffect1: The {n} parts in the kit go with it
confirm.deleteKitEffect2: Job cards you already made from it keep their lines and their costs
confirm.deleteKitItemIntro: It stays on any job card you've already made from “{kit}”.
confirm.deleteLicenceIntro: This is one of the papers FleetWise watches the expiry date on for {machine}.
confirm.deleteLicenceEffect1: You stop being warned before it runs out
confirm.deleteLicenceEffect2: It disappears from the compliance card and the expiry list
confirm.deleteBudgetIntro: This is the spending target you set for {machine}.
confirm.deleteBudgetEffect1: The budget-vs-spend comparison for this period goes away
confirm.deleteBudgetEffect2: What you actually spent is untouched — that comes from the job cards
confirm.deleteFineEffect1: The nomination deadline stops being tracked — miss it and the fine stays with the farm
confirm.deleteFineEffect2: It comes off the fines list and the compliance report
confirm.deletePartIntro: Job cards that already use this part keep their lines and their costs.
confirm.deletePartEffect1: Nobody can pick it when adding a line to a job card
confirm.deletePartnerIntro: This only takes them off your list — it does not cancel work they are busy with.
confirm.deletePartnerEffect1: They stop appearing when you send work out
confirm.deletePartnerEffect2: If they have a login, it keeps working until you say otherwise
confirm.deleteTemplateIntro: This is a Rapid Rise template every farm can apply.
confirm.deleteTemplateEffect1: No farm can apply it to a machine again
confirm.deleteTemplateEffect2: Machines that already use it keep their service plans
confirm.deleteChecklistTemplateIntro: This is the list of questions people answer when they check a machine.
confirm.deleteChecklistTemplateEffect1: Nobody can start a new check from it
confirm.deleteChecklistTemplateEffect2: Checks already done keep every answer exactly as it was saved
confirm.deleteChecklistInstanceIntro: The answers and photos from {date} go with it.
confirm.removeLineIntro: The job card total goes down by {amount}.

pageInfo.checklistsDoes:
Write the questions once, as a template
Fill one in against a machine, with photos where it matters
Look back at what was checked and when
pageInfo.checklistsWhat: The walk-around questions someone answers before starting a machine.
pageInfo.contractorDoes:
See new requests and what each one is for
Send a quote, then an invoice, without leaving the job
Call or WhatsApp the farmer straight from the job
pageInfo.contractorWhat: Every job the farms you work for have sent you, across all of them, in one list.
pageInfo.dashboardDoes:
See which machines are overdue for a service or standing broken
Open the thing itself by tapping the line that names it
See what the fleet has cost you this month
pageInfo.dashboardNote: If this screen is empty, there is genuinely nothing waiting for you.
pageInfo.dashboardWhat: Everything that needs a decision today, worst first, so you never have to go looking for trouble.
pageInfo.driverDoes:
Say something is broken
Write down the hours off the clock
Say you put in diesel
pageInfo.driverNote: You can also just hold your phone to the sticker on the machine.
pageInfo.driverWhat: The four things you need on a machine, and what happened to what you reported.
pageInfo.faultsDoes:
Report something that is wrong, with a photo or a voice note
Turn a problem into a job card so a mechanic can work on it
Mark it sorted out when it is fixed
pageInfo.faultsNote: Drivers can report problems from the QR sticker on the machine without logging in.
pageInfo.faultsWhat: Everything that has been reported as broken, worst first.
pageInfo.finesDoes:
Capture a fine against a vehicle and an offence date
Name the driver before the deadline
See what is still outstanding
pageInfo.finesNote: Naming the driver is a legal deadline under AARTO — the date is shown on each fine.
pageInfo.finesWhat: Fines against farm vehicles, and who was driving.
pageInfo.fuelDoes:
Record a delivery into a tank
Record diesel drawn for a machine
See litres per hour per machine, and anything that looks like a leak or theft
pageInfo.fuelWhat: What has gone into the tank, what has come out, and which machines are drinking more than they should.
pageInfo.inboxDoes:
Accept a price so the contractor can start
Approve a bill once you are happy the work is done
See what is holding each machine up
pageInfo.inboxNote: Nothing is paid because you tapped here — approving records your decision, it does not move money.
pageInfo.inboxWhat: Money decisions from your contractors — prices to accept and bills to approve.
pageInfo.jobcardsDoes:
Start a job card against a machine
Add parts and labour as you go
Approve it when the work is finished, which locks it
pageInfo.jobcardsNote: Once a job card is approved it cannot be edited — that is what makes the cost history trustworthy.
pageInfo.jobcardsWhat: The record of work done on a machine — the parts, the hours and what it cost.
pageInfo.machineDoes:
Write down a new hour or kilometre reading
Set up its service plan, or apply a template
Print its QR sticker so anyone can report a problem without logging in
pageInfo.machineWhat: Everything known about this machine: what it is, what it costs, what has been done to it, and what is due.
pageInfo.machinesDoes:
Add a machine, or import your whole list from a spreadsheet
Filter by type, status, cost centre or department
Open a machine to see its history, services, costs and QR sticker
pageInfo.machinesNote: A machine with no service plan shows a prompt to set one up — that is what makes service dates work.
pageInfo.machinesWhat: Every machine on the farm, with how it is doing and when it was last read.
pageInfo.notificationsDoes:
Read what has happened since you were last here
Turn phone notifications on for this device
Choose the hours we may not disturb you
pageInfo.notificationsWhat: Everything FleetWise has told you, and how it is allowed to tell you.
pageInfo.onboardingDoes:
Get your machines in
Give each one a service plan
Print the QR stickers — this is the step that makes everything else easy
pageInfo.onboardingWhat: The few things worth doing first, so the rest of FleetWise has something to work with.
pageInfo.partnersDoes:
Save a contractor with their phone, WhatsApp and area
Call or WhatsApp them straight from here
Connect one so they can see the jobs you send them
pageInfo.partnersWhat: The farm's contacts — mechanics, auto electricians, parts suppliers, tow trucks.
pageInfo.partsDoes:
Add a part with its number, supplier and usual price
Pull a part straight onto a job card instead of retyping it
Build service kits so a 250-hour service is one tap
pageInfo.partsWhat: The parts you buy, what they usually cost, and who sells them.
pageInfo.reportsDoes:
Choose a period and see cost per machine, per hour and per kilometre
See which machines break most often
Download any of it as a spreadsheet
pageInfo.reportsWhat: The numbers behind the fleet — what things cost, what breaks, and what is being used.
pageInfo.settingsDoes:
Set how early a service should be called due
Set quiet hours so nobody is messaged at night
Choose friendly or professional wording for yourself
pageInfo.settingsWhat: How FleetWise behaves for this farm — when it warns you, and in what words.
pageInfo.teamDoes:
Invite a manager, mechanic or driver by email
Change what someone is allowed to do
Export or erase a person's data if they ask
pageInfo.teamNote: Drivers do not need an account to report a problem — the QR sticker is enough.
pageInfo.teamWhat: Everyone who can use FleetWise on this farm, and what each of them may see.
pageInfo.workDoes:
Ask a contractor for a repair, a quote or an inspection
See their quote and their invoice in one place
Turn finished work into a job card so it counts towards the machine's cost
pageInfo.workWhat: Jobs you have sent to an outside workshop, and where each one has got to.
pageInfo.installWhat: Put FleetWise on the phone itself, so it opens without the browser and keeps working where there is no signal.
pageInfo.installDoes:
Install it straight from this page — there is no file and no app store
See what still works when the signal drops
Understand how what you capture offline gets sent later
pageInfo.documentsWhat: Every quote and bill your contractors have sent you, in one place.
pageInfo.documentsDoes:
Say yes or no to a quote
See what you still owe and to whom
Download any document as a PDF
Record a payment you have made
Attach a bill you were handed on paper
pageInfo.documentsNote: Accepting a quote does not pay anything — the contractor still has to invoice you.
pageInfo.documentsPartnerWhat: What you have quoted and billed, across every farm you work for.
pageInfo.documentsPartnerDoes:
Build a quote line by line and send it
Turn an accepted quote into an invoice
Record payments as they come in
Attach a document you made in your own system
Download anything as a PDF on your letterhead
pageInfo.documentsPartnerNote: Attaching your own documents works on every plan. Building them here is part of Managed.
pageInfo.partnerSettingsWhat: Your name, your numbers, your colours — what customers see on everything you send.
pageInfo.partnerSettingsDoes:
Set the name and registration numbers on your documents
Add your banking details so farmers can pay you
Upload your logo and pick your colours
Choose how long a quote stands and how long you give to pay
pageInfo.partnerSettingsNote: Changes apply to new documents. Ones you have already sent keep the look they had.
pageInfo.clientsWhat: Your whole customer book — not only the farms that found you on FleetWise.
pageInfo.clientsDoes:
Add any customer, whether or not they use FleetWise
Keep their vehicles written down before they join
Ask a customer to connect their farm to you
Copy your vehicle list into their fleet once they connect
Call, WhatsApp or email straight from the list
pageInfo.clientsNote: Adding someone here gives you no access to their data. That only comes when they connect and say yes.
pageInfo.partnersNote: You choose what each connected contractor can see. They never see your other contractors.
pageInfo.statementsWhat: One customer's account: what they owe you right now, and every invoice, credit and payment that got it there.
pageInfo.statementsDoes:
Pick a customer and a period
See how much is overdue, and by how long
Send the statement as a PDF on your letterhead
Download it as a spreadsheet for your bookkeeper
pageInfo.statementsNote: The balance carries forward — anything owed before the period starts shows as the first line, so the closing figure really is what they owe.
pageInfo.correctionsWhat: Every change made to a document after it was sent, newest first — with the reason, the person, and what the amount was before.
pageInfo.correctionsDoes:
See at a glance whether anyone has been reducing totals
Open the document a change was made to
Read the reason it was given
pageInfo.correctionsNote: This log cannot be edited or deleted by anyone, including the person who made the change. That is what makes editing safe.

install.title: Put FleetWise on this phone
install.subtitle: So it opens like any other app — and keeps working where there is no signal.
install.dismissed: No problem. The button stays here if you change your mind.
install.alreadyInstalled: FleetWise is installed on this device.
install.why:
It opens from your home screen, without the browser in the way
It still opens in a shed or a far land where there is no signal
What you capture offline is kept and sent the moment you have signal again
It takes no space worth worrying about — there is nothing to download
install.noFileTitle: There is no file to download
install.noFile: FleetWise installs straight from this page — there is no app store, no APK and nothing to copy onto the phone. That is also why it updates itself: you are never on an old version.
install.iosSteps:
Tap the Share button at the bottom of Safari
Scroll down and tap “Add to Home Screen”
Tap “Add” — FleetWise is now on your home screen
install.otherSteps:
Open the browser menu (the three dots)
Tap “Install app” or “Add to Home screen”
Confirm — FleetWise is now on your home screen
install.offline:
Opening the app and seeing what you looked at last
Reporting a problem on a machine
Writing down hours or kilometres
Recording diesel you put in
install.offlineNote: Anything you capture without signal is kept on the phone and sent on its own the moment you are back in range. You do not have to remember to do anything.

tour.welcomeBody: This keeps track of every machine on the farm — when it was serviced, what broke, and what it cost you. Six short steps and you will know your way around. You can stop at any time.
tour.machinesBody: Every tractor, bakkie, harvester and implement goes in here once. If you already have a list on a spreadsheet, import it instead of typing it again.
tour.qrBody: Each machine gets a sticker. Anyone can hold a phone to it and report a problem or write down the hours — no login, no account, no training. This is the step that makes the rest of FleetWise work on its own.
tour.faultsBody: Problems reported from the stickers land here, worst first. You turn one into a job card when someone is going to work on it.
tour.jobcardsBody: A job card records what was done to a machine — the parts, the hours and the cost. Approve it when the work is finished and it locks, so the cost history stays honest.
tour.moneyBody: Everything above adds up here: cost per machine, per hour, per kilometre, and which machines break most often. This is the part that pays for itself.
tour.installBody: Install FleetWise so it opens from the home screen and keeps working in a shed or a far land. Whatever is captured without signal is sent on its own when the signal comes back.
tour.helpBody: Every screen has a “What is this?” button next to its name that explains what the screen is for. You can start this walkthrough again from there whenever you like.
tour.driverWelcomeBody: This is for the people who work on the machines. Four things, no paperwork. It takes a minute to show you.
tour.driverScanTitle: Hold your phone to the sticker
tour.driverScanBody: Every machine has a sticker on it. Hold your phone to it and the machine comes up on the screen — you do not have to log in or find it in a list.
tour.driverFaultBody: Broken, leaking, or making a noise — press one button, take a photo if it helps, and the farm office sees it. You can talk into it instead of typing.
tour.driverHoursBody: Read the number off the clock and type it in. That is what tells the office when the machine is due for a service, so it does not break in the middle of a season.
tour.contractorWelcomeBody: Every farm you work for sends you jobs in one place, so you are not chasing five different WhatsApp groups. A minute to show you around.
tour.contractorWorkTitle: All your jobs, all your farms
tour.contractorWorkBody: New requests arrive here with the vehicle, what is wrong and how urgent it is. One list across every farm that has connected you.
tour.contractorQuoteBody: Send a price from inside the job. When the farmer accepts it you do the work, then send the invoice from the same screen. You can call or WhatsApp them without leaving it.
tour.contractorDocumentsBody: Build a quote line by line and send it, turn an accepted quote into an invoice, and record payments as they land. Already invoice somewhere else? Attach that document instead — it works on every plan.
tour.contractorBrandBody: Your name, registration and VAT numbers, banking details, logo and colours. Everything you send goes out on your letterhead, not ours.

doc.title: Quotes & invoices
doc.leadPartner: Everything you have quoted and billed, across every farm you work for.
doc.leadFarm: What your contractors have quoted you, and what they have billed you.
doc.newSubjectHint: A short line the farmer will recognise — “Service on the New Holland”.
doc.needsYouPartner: Waiting on you or on them
doc.emptyPartnerBody: Start one from a customer, or attach a document you made in your own system.
doc.emptyFarmBody: When a contractor sends you a quote or a bill, it lands here.
doc.notesHint: Anything they should read before they decide.
doc.sendExplains: Once you send it, the wording and the totals are fixed — it becomes a record of what you told them.
doc.sentFlash: Sent. They can see it now.
doc.deleteDraftBody: Nothing was sent, so there is nothing to keep. The lines go with it.
doc.convertedFlash: Invoice started from the quote — check it, then send it.
doc.cancelBody: It stays on the record as cancelled, and stops counting against the farm's costs.
doc.decideTitle: Do you want this work done?
doc.acceptBody: The contractor will be told you have accepted. No money moves until they invoice you.
doc.declineReasonHint: “Too expensive” and “we sorted it ourselves” lead them to very different next steps.
doc.paymentsUpgrade: Recording payments is part of the Managed plan.
doc.uploadBody: Attach the quote or invoice your own system produced. Your customer sees it here, and it counts towards their costs — you carry on invoicing however you already do.
doc.uploadTotalHint: The amount printed on it, VAT included.
doc.uploadFileHint: A PDF or a photo of it.
doc.uploadedBody: This document was made in the contractor's own system.
doc.upgradeTitle: Want to build quotes and invoices here?
doc.upgradeBody: The Managed plan adds line-by-line quotes and invoices, converting a quote into a bill, and recording payments.
doc.upgradeKeep: You keep everything you have now — attaching your own documents stays part of your plan.
doc.upgradeNeeded: That is part of the Managed plan.

uploadError.failed: That did not go through. Try again.
uploadError.missing_total: Type the total that is printed on it.
uploadError.upload_failed: The file would not upload. Try a smaller one.
uploadError.forbidden: You are not allowed to do that.

doc.oneOffHint: Nothing gets saved to your client book. Just type who it is for and carry on.
doc.billToAddressHint: Needed on a tax invoice over R5 000.
doc.billToVatHint: Without this they cannot claim the VAT back.
doc.changeBilling: Their details are different this time
doc.theirReferenceHint: Optional — what they call this job on their side.
doc.refundHint: If you have to return money to this customer, record it here so their account shows it left.
doc.refundInCredit: They have paid more than this invoice comes to. In credit:
doc.refundBody: This records money going back to the customer. It shows on their statement on the day you paid it out.
doc.refundAmount: How much are you paying back?
doc.writtenOffFlash: Written off. It has come off what they owe you.
doc.refundTooBig: You cannot pay back more than has been paid on this invoice.

partnerSettings.title: My business
partnerSettings.lead: This is what your customers see on every quote and invoice you send.
partnerSettings.name: Business name
partnerSettings.tradingNameHint: Leave blank to use your business name.
partnerSettings.vatNoHint: Leave blank if you are not VAT registered.
partnerSettings.areaHint: The towns or district you travel to.
partnerSettings.bankingHint: Printed on your invoices so a farmer can pay you without phoning to ask.
partnerSettings.brandPrimaryHint: Used for the header on your documents.
partnerSettings.poweredByHint: Turn this off if you would rather the document showed only your name.
partnerSettings.termsHint: Printed at the bottom of every document.
partnerSettings.logoHint: A PNG, JPEG or SVG. It sits at the top of every document.
partnerSettings.removeLogoBody: Your documents go back to showing your name on its own.
partnerSettings.logoError: That image would not open. Try another one.
partnerSettings.prefixHint: So your first quote is QTE-0001.
partnerSettings.vatRegisteredHint: Turn this off if you are below the threshold. Your documents will show no VAT at all.
partnerSettings.vatNotRegisteredNote: Your documents show no VAT. The rate is kept in case you register later.

clients.title: My clients
clients.lead: Your whole customer book — the farms already on FleetWise with you, and everybody else.
clients.waitingHint: They decide — you'll see their fleet the moment they say yes.
clients.alreadyConnected: Already connected, not in your book
clients.alreadyConnectedHint: These farms added you themselves. Add them here so you have one list.
clients.emptyBody: Add your customers here — you don't need them on FleetWise to keep their details and their vehicles.
clients.addHint: Anyone you work for. If they're on FleetWise you can ask them to connect afterwards.
clients.name: Business or farm name
clients.emailHint: Needed if you want to ask them to connect on FleetWise.
clients.notConnectedBody: This client isn't connected to you on FleetWise, so you're keeping their details here yourself.
clients.needEmail: Add their email address first — that's how the request reaches them.
clients.askedBody: We've asked them to connect. Only they can accept it.
clients.askedFlash: Asked. They'll see it when they next open FleetWise.
clients.askedShare: If they're not on FleetWise yet, send them the invite yourself:
clients.inviteMessage: I keep your vehicles and service history on FleetWise. Join and we'll both see the same records: https://fleetwise.app
clients.syncBody: You have {n} vehicles written down here that aren't in their fleet yet.
clients.syncConfirmTitle: Copy these vehicles into their fleet?
clients.syncConsequence: They become real vehicles the farm owns — everyone there will see them.
clients.vehiclesHint: Your own notes on what they run. Keep them here until they're on FleetWise.
clients.vehiclesConnectedHint: Your own notes. Once copied across they become part of the farm's real fleet.
clients.removeClientTitle: Remove this client from your book?
clients.removeClientConsequence: Your notes and their vehicle list go with it.
clients.removeClientKeepsLink: You stay connected to their farm — this only removes your own record.
clients.connectedFlash: Already connected — this client is now linked to their farm.
clients.syncPartial: {n} copied. Some could not be added — try again, the rest are still waiting.
clients.billingHint: Used on every quote and invoice you raise for them, so you never retype it.
clients.vatNoHint: Without this they cannot claim the VAT back on your invoices.
clients.termsHint: Leave blank to use your own default.
clients.creditLimitHint: Optional — just a note to yourself.

access.title: What they can see
access.baseline: Without any of these, they can see the vehicles they are working on for you, the faults and jobs on those vehicles, and the requests you send them. Nothing else.
access.vehiclesHint: Every vehicle, not only the ones they are working on. Useful for someone who services everything.
access.historyHint: Past readings and service plans on the vehicles they can see.
access.costsHint: Prices, budgets, fuel and job-card amounts — including what you paid other people.
access.teamHint: The names, emails and phone numbers of everyone on your farm.
access.neverPartners: Your other contractors are never visible to them, whatever you choose here.
access.disconnectBody: {name} will lose access to this farm straight away.
access.disconnectConsequence: They keep the quotes and invoices they already sent you, and you keep yours.
access.disconnectFootnote: You can connect them again later.

correct.title: Something wrong with this one?
correct.intro: Sent documents stay as they are — that is what makes them a record. Here is how you fix a mistake without pretending it never happened.
correct.reasonHint: Shown on the credit note, so your customer knows why.
correct.shouldNotExist: It should never have gone out
correct.shouldNotExistHint: Wrong customer, or a duplicate. The document and its number stay on file; the money comes off.
correct.voidBody: This stops the money counting. The document stays on file with your reason on it, so anyone looking later can see what happened.
correct.voidConsequence1: It comes off what the customer owes you.
correct.voidConsequence2: If a copy is already out there, it will still say cancelled when they open the link.
correct.voidReasonHint: A few words is enough. This is what you will read in six months.
correct.overchargedHint: A credit note puts the money back. Use this when they have already paid — the refund needs to show as its own thing.
correct.underchargedHint: A debit note adds the difference to the same job, so it reads as part of that invoice on their statement instead of turning up as a mystery charge.
correct.neverPaying: They are never going to pay
correct.neverPayingHint: Write it off. The invoice stays on their statement exactly as it was — the work was done — but it stops counting as money you are owed, and we stop chasing it.
correct.writeOffBody: Use this when you have given up on collecting. It is not the same as cancelling — the bill was correct, the money is just not coming.
correct.writeOffConsequence1: It stops counting as outstanding, and stops appearing in your overdue totals.
correct.writeOffConsequence2: It stays on the customer’s statement, with a matching line that clears the balance.
correct.writeOffConsequence3: The version before this is kept, with your reason, and cannot be deleted.
correct.writeOffReason: Why are you writing it off?
correct.writeOffReasonHint: For example: business closed down, or three years of no contact.
correct.writeOffReasonMissing: Say why you are writing it off — a few words is enough.

email.title: Send it to them
email.never: {name} has not been emailed this yet.
email.ccHint: Optional — a second address that should also get it.
email.messageHint: Optional. It goes at the top of the email.
email.failed: That did not send. Try again in a moment.
email.notConfigured: Email is not switched on for this system yet. Download the PDF and send it yourself for now.
email.badAddress: That does not look like an email address.

statement.title: Statements
statement.tagline: What each customer owes you, and how it got there.
statement.ageingHint: Counted from the day each invoice fell due, oldest first.
statement.emptyBody: No invoices, credits or payments between these dates. Try a wider window.
statement.noneBody: Statements are per customer. Add someone to your client book, or connect to a farm, and their account will build itself as you invoice them.
statement.sendHint: Optional. It goes at the top of the email, above the balance.

pubDoc.decide: What would you like to do?
pubDoc.decideHint: Accepting tells them to go ahead with the work.
pubDoc.yourNameHint: So they know who said yes.
pubDoc.declineReason: Anything you want to tell them?
pubDoc.toldFlash: They have been told to look out for it.
pubDoc.closedFlash: This one has already been dealt with.
pubDoc.nameFlash: Please put your name in so they know who accepted.
pubDoc.voided: This {label} has been cancelled and is not payable.
pubDoc.askThem: Ask them how they would like to be paid.
pubDoc.paidRefHint: Optional — it helps them find it on their bank statement.
pubDoc.creditExplains: This credit note takes {amount} off invoice {number}. There is nothing to pay on this document.

revise.title: Change this document
revise.intro: You can fix what is on it. Every version is kept, with your reason, so you and your customer can always see what it said before.
revise.reason: What are you changing, and why?
revise.reasonHint: Your customer can read this. A few plain words is enough.
revise.items: What they are being charged for
revise.inclVat: The prices I typed already include VAT at {pct}
revise.belowPaid: That is less than they have already paid. Use a credit note instead, so the money going back shows up on its own.
revise.keptOnFile: The current version of {number} is saved before this replaces it.
revise.historyIntro: Every version, with who changed it and why.
revise.savedFlash: Saved. The version before this is on file.
revise.reasonMissing: Say what you are changing and why — your customer can read it.
revise.emptyDocument: A document needs at least one line.

corrections.title: Corrections log
corrections.tagline: Every change ever made to a document that had already gone out.
corrections.emptyBody: When someone changes a document that has already been sent, it shows up here — with the reason, who did it and what the amount was before.
